questions.q: What is the real purpose of the `cause_notes` field on a Problem record?
options: A journal field for documenting investigation findings incrementally as they develop
A field reserved only for the final, permanent fix
A reference field pointing at the affected CI
A field that is auto-filled by the Incident state model
questions.explain: cause_notes tells the ongoing story of the investigation; fix_notes is reserved separately for the eventual answer.

questions.q: Why are `cause_notes` and `fix_notes` kept as two separate fields rather than one combined field?
options: So a reader never has to scroll through weeks of investigative dead ends to find the actual resolution
ServiceNow does not allow two notes fields on the same table
Because Incident records require both fields to be identical
There is no real reason; they could be merged with no loss of clarity
questions.explain: Separating the investigation narrative from the final fix keeps the record usable for someone who just needs the answer.

questions.q: What does the `root_cause` field often reference in a real implementation?
options: A `cmdb_ci` record or a category value indicating what was actually at fault
The original Incident that triggered the Problem
The assignment group handling the investigation
The SLA definition tied to the affected service
questions.explain: Making root cause a structured reference (not free text) makes it reportable — e.g. which CI causes the most Problems.

questions.q: What is the real Problem state model described in this lesson?
options: New, Root Cause Analysis, Fix in Progress, Resolved, Closed
New, In Progress, Resolved, Closed (identical to Incident)
Open, Escalated, Pending, Closed
Draft, Under Review, Approved, Implemented
questions.explain: Problem's state model mirrors Incident's general shape but adds investigative states that reflect its slower, deeper purpose.

questions.q: Why is it correct, not a flaw, for a Problem to sit in 'Root Cause Analysis' for weeks while related Incidents keep getting opened and closed quickly?
options: Incident Management is optimized for fast restoration even with a temporary fix, while Problem Management is investigative work to find out why it happened at all
It means the Problem process is broken and needs to be redesigned
Incidents should never be closed while a related Problem is open
Root Cause Analysis should always take less time than Incident resolution
questions.explain: The two processes are intentionally running at different speeds because they're solving different problems — speed versus depth.
